title: Peloton product study → FORM / health v4
scope: Public official website and product imagery; not an authenticated account audit.
mode: Built-in image_gen. Five static bitmap concepts. Viewer only is HTML.
versioning: v3 and v2 preserved. Finance and to-do unchanged.

observations.observed: Dark navigation, dominant moving human imagery, white pill actions, moderate sentence-case headings. The imagery carries the energy.
observations.decision: Full-width movement photography and generous editorial pacing for the website.

observations.observed: Published app composition shows black surfaces, violet week markers, orange/blue/magenta activity targets, prominent instructor imagery and persistent bottom navigation.
observations.decision: Graphite application foundation, visible weekly rhythm and one next session. Compress metrics into an open strip to meet the user's no-card-wall constraint.

observations.observed: A focused exercise screen gives the demonstration most of the space; time, sets, reps and next move remain close to the action. Progress charts are spare and contextual.
observations.decision: The session and its actionable next step lead. The web app reviews one workout with readable units and a supporting time series.

observations.observed: Quiet grey stage, large human movement, compact workout customization. Duration and muscle focus are directly tied to the workout.
observations.decision: Maintain a clear plan → session → review sequence instead of unrelated dashboard metrics.

observations.observed: Large athlete imagery in a sparse field; training and movement feedback are associated with a person and exercise rather than abstract gauges.
observations.decision: Use natural movement photography and restrained supporting measurements, without invented readiness or clinical scores.

observations.observed: The website shares Bike+'s generous neutral stage, rounded actions and calm typography.
observations.decision: Keep a coherent design family across product sizes; do not use unrelated stylistic treatments for each screen.

observations.observed: Personal plans, exercise selection and contextual guidance connect the product story. Dark translucent overlays sit against rich movement photography.
observations.decision: A prominent next planned session connects progress to action. A subtle photo fade supports contrast; no decorative glass or glow.

interpretation: The charcoal/violet FORM direction is a selective interpretation of the public app references, not a claim that every Peloton product uses this palette. The site retains dark/light editorial chapter changes. No logo or real instructor is reproduced.
style: Original fitness tracker named FORM, informed by a visual study of current Peloton App, Strength+, Bike+, Row, Tread and Peloton IQ. Matte graphite #15171B and near-black #0B0C0F, off-white type, subtle charcoal divisions, gentle 14px corners. Contemporary readable neo-grotesk typography, medium weight, sentence case, tabular metrics. Normal width typography, no condensed display fonts. Photography is the hero: richly detailed editorial real human movement, premium dark studio with soft light, natural skin, calm confidence, no dystopian neon. White pill primary controls. Purple #8068EF is reserved for completed days and progress; small peach accents for time. Accent colors are functional, not glowing. Cohesive open sections and an uninterrupted weekly rhythm rather than a wall of dashboard cards. No banking ledger aesthetic, no white dashboard, no neon-green recovery dial, no circular score as centerpiece, no chrome/gloss/3D bevels, no generic SaaS gradient blobs. Icons are small consistent line icons. All text crisp and readable with deliberate padding. This is an original concept, not a fake official Peloton screenshot; use FORM wordmark, no Peloton logo or real instructor identity.

limitations: Public marketing compositions contain interface examples, not directly captured signed-in apps.
Photographs, names and training data in the concepts are fictional.
Charts are illustrative raster drawings; the review page implements no tracker functionality.
acceptance: Progress has 3 completed workouts totaling 140 minutes.
75% weekly workout target, Sunday mobility still planned.
No eight-card dashboard; one integrated time axis and an obvious next action.
New visual family distinct from white Ramp finance and old neon WHOOP.
